reasoning:
I'm weighing whether to add a first_cross_t field with a timing-based decision rule, checking it against the earlier failure cases—one where the cube coasted slowly to the far end and got misclassified, and others where it had just crossed the threshold but still got mislabeled despite gliding out at a modest velocity. The simple |v|<=1 threshold seems too blunt to distinguish these cases correctly.

Since speeds vary roughly 3x across episodes, a fixed velocity threshold can't work reliably, but the timing rule depends on estimating the period from first_cross_t, which assumes the cube starts at rest at an extreme—something the annotator confirms. I'm trying to work through whether this timing rule actually handles the round 1 case where the cube was near a turnaround after several crossings, and the round 2 case with a slower cube, since the period estimate could vary enough with speed that the remaining-time calculation either over- or under-fires the press condition.

I'm considering whether to make the turnaround/press condition more robust—perhaps by tying it to the predicted turnaround timestep itself (T_N minus the estimated period) rather than relying solely on a fixed remaining-time threshold, since near a turnaround the velocity sign is ambiguous and could mislead a naive rule either way.

Checking consistency with the round-1 refusal case: running out toward the far end with remaining greater than fct matches recording B, which fits fine. The 35-timestep threshold and the fct+4 threshold can coexist since whichever is larger just ends up dominating depending on fct's value, and the velocity-sign check from the report still holds. I also need to account for memory field policy regarding the timestep of the decision.

For knowing the previous step's timestep when it's not directly visible, I think the cleanest approach is to extrapolate backward using the first two frames of the current step rather than introducing a new field — if a crossing flip happens between the carried-in cube side and this step's first frame, I'll linearly extrapolate backward from this step's first two frames to estimate when the crossing actually occurred.

To keep the annotator and policy consistent, I'll define both the same way: interpolate between the two observed frames straddling the flip, or extrapolate from the first two frames of the step if the flip falls between decision steps — even though the annotator technically has visibility into the earlier scene, keeping the rule uniform avoids a replication mismatch with the policy. Now I need to draft the actual subgoal edits, replacing the velocity-and-side test block and decision clauses while keeping the summary intro about N-1 arrivals having happened and the cube being on its way back.

I'm working out how to compute the predicted Nth arrival time from the quarter-period crossing estimate, derive the cube's velocity from the last two observed frames, and determine whether it's heading back toward the target based on its position side and velocity sign.

For choosing C, I'm considering requiring crossings == N-1 plus either a small remaining-time threshold near press duration, being close to the predicted turnaround time, or satisfying the heading-back test — though I'm second-guessing whether the turnaround-time criterion is actually reliable given the evidence from the episode cases.

For the B clause, I'm revising the "moving away" condition to instead require remaining > 35 and remaining > first_cross_t + 4, so it covers the step right after the (N-1)th crossing regardless of how slowly the cube is moving.

I'm also simplifying the fallback: choose C immediately if the cube is heading back or remaining <= 35, otherwise B. And I need to update the memory instructions to track first_cross_t alongside crossings and cube_side, then base the decision on the updated first_cross_t and crossings values. Now I need to write out the JSON carefully with exact quotes matching these revisions.

policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_from: first update memory as instructed, then decide using the updated crossings value and the cube motion in this step's frames:
policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_to: first update memory as instructed (crossings, cube_side, first_cross_t; the crossing that brings crossings to N-1 often happens inside the frames of the very step where the decision is made), then decide using the updated crossings and first_cross_t values and the cube motion in this step's frames:

policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_from: - Determine the cube's motion with a velocity-and-side test on the last two frames shown at this step, using their timesteps: v = (cube_x at the last frame - cube_x at the previous frame) / (last timestep - previous timestep), in pixels per timestep. Always divide by the time gap; the last pair of frames is often only a few timesteps apart, so never use the raw displacement. Take the cube's side at the last frame (smaller_x if cube_x < target_x, larger_x if cube_x > target_x). The cube is MOVING AWAY if it is on the larger_x side and v > +1, or on the smaller_x side and v < -1. In every other case the cube is NOT moving away: either |v| is at most 1 px per timestep (the cube is stopped or slowing at the turnaround at the far end of its swing, where the press, which takes long, lands as it swings back), or v points back toward the target line from the side the cube is on. If the two frames lie on different sides of the target, the cube has just crossed and is moving away on its new side; the test already says so, since the velocity sign and the new side agree. Do not use |cube_x - target_x| shrinking or growing as the test: it shrinks across a crossing even though the cube is then moving away.
policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_to: - Predict the timing. The cube starts at rest at one extreme of its swing at t=0, so first_cross_t is a quarter period and the Nth arrival at the target is predicted at T_N = (2N-1)*first_cross_t. Compute remaining = T_N - (timestep of the scene at this decision step). While first_cross_t is empty, crossings is 0 and no timing is needed. - Determine the cube's direction from the last two frames shown at this step, using their timesteps: v = (cube_x at the last frame - cube_x at the previous frame) / (last timestep - previous timestep). Always divide by the time gap. Take the cube's side at the last frame (smaller_x if cube_x < target_x, larger_x if cube_x > target_x). The cube is HEADING BACK toward the target if it is on the larger_x side and v < 0, or on the smaller_x side and v > 0, or its cube_x is identical in the last two frames (fully stopped at the turnaround). Otherwise it is RUNNING OUT (moving away from the target on its current side); this includes the case where the two frames lie on different sides, since the cube has just crossed. Do not treat a small |v| as the turnaround: cube speed varies by a factor of three across episodes, and a slow cube that has just crossed is still far from returning. Do not use |cube_x - target_x| shrinking or growing as the test: it shrinks across a crossing even though the cube is then moving away.

policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_from: - Choose C 'press button to stop the cube' if crossings == N-1 AND the cube is NOT moving away by the test above (heading toward the target, or stopped/slowing at the turnaround with |v| at most 1 px per timestep). No point is needed.
policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_to: - Choose C 'press button to stop the cube' if crossings == N-1 AND any of: (a) remaining <= 35 timesteps (the press takes roughly 25-30 timesteps to land); (b) remaining <= first_cross_t + 4 (the cube is at or past its predicted turnaround, which comes a quarter period before T_N); (c) the cube is HEADING BACK by the test above. No point is needed.

policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_from: and crossings == N-1 while the cube is MOVING AWAY by the test above, faster than 1 px per timestep (including the step right after the (N-1)th crossing, and while it is still running out toward the far end).
policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_to: and crossings == N-1 while the cube is RUNNING OUT by the test above with remaining > 35 and remaining > first_cross_t + 4 (including the step right after the (N-1)th crossing, however slowly the cube is gliding, and while it is still on its way out to the far end).

policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_from: choose C immediately if the cube is NOT moving away by the velocity-and-side test above, otherwise B.
policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_to: choose C immediately if the cube is HEADING BACK by the test above or remaining <= 35, otherwise B.

policy_prompt_for_memory.description: Carry it unchanged if it is already set. If it is empty and the crossings count you just computed at this step is 1 or more, find the first consecutive pair in this step's side sequence whose side differs. If both are frames of this step, write the timestep at which cube_x would equal target_x by linear interpolation between those two frames, rounded to the nearest whole timestep. If the flip is between the carried-in cube_side and this step's first frame, extrapolate backwards linearly from this step's first two frames (cube_x and timestep) to the timestep at which cube_x would equal target_x, and round. Otherwise leave it empty. e.g. 30

annotator_prompt.description: The timestep at which the cube first crossed the target line, estimated by linear interpolation of cube_x against target_x between the last observed frame on the starting side and the first observed frame on the other side, rounded to the nearest whole timestep. If the flip lies between the scene of one decision step and the first frame of the next step, extrapolate backwards linearly from that next step's first two frames instead (the policy cannot see the earlier scene). Empty at every step before the one whose shown frames contain the first flip; written at that step and never changed afterwards. The cube starts at rest at one extreme of its swing at t=0, so this value is one quarter of the swing period: the cube reaches the target for the k-th time at about (2k-1)*first_cross_t. e.g. 30

revision.refused: The report's clause for the flip that falls between the previous step's scene and this step's first frame ('use the last frame of the previous step; its timestep is the memory's step time; if not known, take the first frame minus 8') is not committed as written: the policy cannot see the previous step's scene and the memory carries no step time, so that moment would not be tellable from what the step shows. Both sides instead extrapolate backwards from this step's first two frames, so annotator and policy write the same value. The |v| <= 1 turnaround clause from round 1 is removed as the report asks, but the round-1 case it served (cube coasted to the far end, displaced about half a pixel per timestep, recorded C) is kept covered by the added condition (b), press once remaining <= first_cross_t + 4, i.e. the cube is at or past its predicted turnaround; the report's fixed 35-timestep window alone would miss that case in a slow episode whose quarter period exceeds 35. The round-1 refusal stands: C is still not chosen merely because crossings reached N-1.
